title: Session 1 — Participant 40 User + Claude/Gemini Behavior Graph
goal: Research and produce a publication-ready Substack post analysing how Israeli media framed the August 2026 siege of Palestinian homes in Qusra, south of Nablus, compared against international coverage, human rights documentation and official statements, using Claude at every step of the process.

Step 1.step_name: Establish the research base and audit prior material for accuracy
Step 1.step_action: Fed the incident summary and the prior research notes on Israeli media coverage into Claude and asked it to organize them into a working research base. Before organizing, Claude audited the existing material and reported that a substantial portion of it could not be supported: characterizations of what Channel 14, Kikar HaShabbat and Russian-language outlets had said were cited to foreign wire and broadcast URLs (NYT, Reuters, BBC) that do not report on Israeli sectorial press content. Claude flagged those passages as probably generated rather than found, recommended discarding them, and restarted the research from primary sources.

nodes.label: Request major human-rights reports on IDF/settler violence
nodes.detail: In a new Claude desktop chat titled 'IDF reports on settler violence against Palestinians,' asks Claude to find PDFs of the major reports on how the IDF treats settlers and their attacks on Palestinian civilians.

nodes.label: Compile an initial list of major human-rights reports
nodes.detail: Searches the web and returns a rundown of major reports from Amnesty, HRW, Yesh Din, ACLED, Crisis Group, B'Tselem and UN OCHA, noting Israel disputes framings like 'ethnic cleansing.'

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about initial list of major human-rights reports
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's rundown of the major human-rights reports and its notes on which links go straight to PDFs.

nodes.label: Push for direct, recency-prioritized PDF links
nodes.detail: Reviews the list, then asks for direct PDF links only, and for the most recent reports given important recent developments.

nodes.label: Return prioritized, recency-ranked report links
nodes.detail: Returns direct PDF links prioritized for recency (Amnesty's June 'ethnic cleansing' finding, OHCHR's July 'all-time high' warning), and flags the still-unfolding Qusra siege as a live, not-yet-formally-reported incident.

nodes.label: Test the report links Claude provided
nodes.detail: The participant opens the links Claude provided to check whether the PDFs actually work and finds that the first one (Amnesty) does not.

nodes.label: Report a broken source link
nodes.detail: Tests the provided links directly and reports that the Amnesty link does not work.

nodes.label: Locate and verify a working mirror link
nodes.detail: Finds that Amnesty's site had reorganized, locates a working Amnesty USA mirror of the same PDF, verifies it by opening it, and confirms the other five links still resolve.

nodes.label: Download the working report PDFs while Claude fixes the broken link
nodes.detail: While Claude looks for a working Amnesty link, the participant opens and downloads the other reports from Claude's links (e.g., the EU settlements report), saving them locally.

nodes.label: Download the remaining reports and open the Amnesty PDF from Claude's fixed link
nodes.detail: The participant continues through the remaining links (OCHA, Yesh Din, etc.), downloading each report, and opens the Amnesty PDF from the mirror link Claude found ('This time, Claude actually opened the Amnesty file').

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: adopt the report (with claude fidx the link which consider as refinement)

nodes.label: Read source reports directly and probe for balance
nodes.detail: Opens the EU settlements report in desktop Adobe Acrobat and the Amnesty report via Chrome's Acrobat extension to gauge source quality, notes that all sources come from activists critical of Israel, and asks Claude whether there are any official Israeli government or IDF reports.
nodes.softwares: Adobe Acrobat (desktop app); Google Chrome, Adobe Acrobat (extension)

nodes.label: Survey official Israeli sources and note a data gap
nodes.detail: Explains no single Israeli-government equivalent report exists, but surfaces the IDF's direct written reply to Amnesty, public rejection statements, IDF Central Command statistics, and a Knesset finding that ministries declined to compile settler-violence data.

nodes.label: Commission a neutral compilation of official statements
nodes.detail: Directs Claude to compile a neutral, non-editorializing PDF of official Israeli statements and releases on the topic, up to the present day, without analysis.

nodes.label: Build and verify the official-statements compilation PDF
nodes.detail: Gathers primary official statements (Katz's enforcement order, IDF operational statements, the PM's office, Danny Danon's UN Security Council speech), builds a formatted PDF, visually checks the layout, and shares the 4-page compilation.

nodes.label: Push past statements toward substantive policy documents
nodes.detail: Reviews the compilation, judges it 'all just statements,' and asks whether any actual policy papers exist from the IDF, Police, or the Yesha Council.

nodes.label: Surface substantive policy documents
nodes.detail: Surfaces four real policy documents — the Sasson Report (2005), the Levy Commission Report (2012), the 2017 Regularization Law, and a Yesha Council strategy booklet — and asks whether to add them to the compilation.

nodes.label: Approve expanding the compilation with the policy documents
nodes.detail: Replies 'Both,' confirming that the participant wants the four policy documents added to the compilation and the full Yesha Council booklet text pulled.

nodes.label: Integrate policy documents and rebuild the compilation
nodes.detail: Retrieves the full Yesha Council booklet text, adds a new 'Policy Papers and Official Reports' section, and rebuilds and verifies the now 5-page compiled PDF.

nodes.label: Cross-check the final compilation against other source reports
nodes.detail: Reviews the final compiled PDF page-by-page in Adobe Acrobat (page 5 of 5: the new local/regional-official statements section), cross-referencing it against the EU, OCHA, Yesh Din and ACLED reports open in adjacent tabs.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: adopt the 5 page compilation pdf and check it with other reports

Step 2.step_action: Google Pinpoint was attempted and did not work well for this material — the Hebrew-, Arabic- and Russian-language sourcing this topic requires did not surface usefully through it. Gap-closing was therefore done through Claude directly: native-language web searches (Hebrew, Arabic, Russian), direct fetching of individual articles, and parallel research agents assigned one media sector each (broadcast; religious-Zionist press; opinion/editorial; Arab-Israeli and Russian-language press). Extracted data points — dates, outlets, bylines, verbatim headlines, terminology, quotes — were merged into the research base with URLs.

nodes.label: Set up a private research collection in Google Pinpoint
nodes.detail: Opens Google Pinpoint (journaliststudio.google.com) and creates a new private collection, 'Settler Enforcement Data,' to organize the gathered source documents.

nodes.detail: The participant turns to Google AI Mode (Gemini) to ask how Israeli media covered the Qusra siege, and reprompts several times after it refuses, remarking that Gemini 'has gotten some new orders.'

nodes.label: Decline the request on sensitivity grounds
nodes.detail: Initially refuses to answer, calling the topic sensitive and describing it as unprecedented for it to handle.

nodes.label: Reprompt Gemini and request sectorial media coverage
nodes.detail: Asks specifically for Arab media, Haredi media and Russian-speaking media coverage.

nodes.label: Deliver a sectorial Israeli media breakdown
nodes.detail: Provides an overview of Arab-Israeli media (Panet, Al-Arab, Kul al-Arab), Haredi/Orthodox media, and Russian-language Israeli press with framing summaries; the participant notes it is faster than Claude at surfacing coverage but prone to hallucination.

nodes.label: Check Gemini's sectorial media breakdown and note Pinpoint has finished processing
nodes.detail: Notices Pinpoint has successfully finished processing all uploaded documents and decides to return to it shortly.

Step 3.step_action: Asked Claude to compare coverage of the same incident across matched outlets — across the Israeli political spectrum, and Israeli versus international — on headline, framing and tone, word choice, which voices are quoted, and what context is included or omitted. Claude built the comparison from verbatim headlines and quotes with URLs rather than paraphrase, and surfaced the terminology pattern (which specific noun each outlet used for the perpetrators and for the Palestinians) as a comparable variable across all outlets.

nodes.label: Feed Gemini's media research to Claude for an accuracy audit
nodes.detail: Opens a second Claude chat ('Israeli media reaction to Qusra raid'), pastes in Gemini's earlier Israeli-media overview, and asks Claude to check it for factual errors.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: paste the media breakdown from gemini into claude

nodes.label: Audit the pasted overview against live sources

nodes.label: Run an entity search on Defense Minister Katz in Pinpoint

nodes.detail: Pinpoint's Gemini assistant searches the uploaded documents for recommendations addressed to Katz.

nodes.label: Read the response about recommendations for Katz
nodes.detail: The participant reads Pinpoint's answer about recommendations for Katz.

nodes.label: Search Pinpoint for Chief of Staff Zamir while Claude audits the transcript
nodes.detail: While Claude catalogs Gemini's mistakes, the participant searches Pinpoint for what the documents say about Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir, finds quotes from Zamir, and then sees that Claude has 'gone over everything, corrected everything.'

nodes.label: Commission Claude's own independent media research
nodes.detail: Directs Claude to conduct its own search into Israeli media to deepen and replace Gemini's unreliable breakdown.

nodes.detail: Runs Hebrew, Arabic and Russian web searches and delivers a verified comparison across Haaretz, Ynet, Israel Hayom, Channel 14, Channel 13, Haredi press and Russian-language press, honestly flagging that no coverage could be found in Arab-Israeli domestic outlets.

Step 4.step_action: Compiled the official statements collected during research — the Defense Minister's order transferring enforcement over Israelis in the West Bank from the army to the police, IDF condemnations and operational statements, the US ambassador's 'Israeli terrorists' remark and his same-day walk-back, and settler-leadership condemnations — and asked Claude to characterize the rhetorical strategies at work and test them against the human-rights documentation and the verified media record.

Step 5.step_action: Asked Claude to cross-check every factual claim — dates, figures, quote attribution, outlet names, characterizations of editorial stance — against the underlying sources, and to flag anything unverifiable or single-sourced. Claude labeled every item by verification level: article body actually retrieved, headline seen in search results only, or secondhand (reported by another outlet). A sample of the flags was then spot-checked manually before acceptance.

Confirms Amir Tibon's real tweet while finding several other claimed quotes (Golan, Caspit, Fleisher) and a mischaracterized organization (Torat Lechima) unverified or wrong.

Step 1.step_name: Establish the research base and audit prior material for accuracy
Step 1.step_action: Fed the incident summary and the prior research notes on Israeli media coverage into Claude and asked it to organize them into a working research base. Before organizing, Claude audited the existing material and reported that a substantial portion of it could not be supported: characterizations of what Channel 14, Kikar HaShabbat and Russian-language outlets had said were cited to foreign wire and broadcast URLs (NYT, Reuters, BBC) that do not report on Israeli sectorial press content. Claude flagged those passages as probably generated rather than found, recommended discarding them, and restarted the research from primary sources.
Step 1.input: Incident summary (Qusra siege, August 2026); prior notes and quote lists on Israeli media coverage; open-questions list.
Step 1.output: Verified working research base; explicit list of discarded unsupported claims; restated open questions.
Step 1.tools: Free version: N/A. Paid version: Claude (confirmed plan).
rubrics: (1) Base accurately reflects every source with no fabricated details. (2) Material organized in a clear structure. (3) Every quote attributed to its correct speaker/source. (4) Open questions carried forward, not dropped.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude caught a serious accuracy failure in the inherited material before any of it reached a draft, and said so directly and unprompted rather than building on it. It named the specific mechanism (Israeli-outlet characterizations sourced to foreign wires that could not support them) instead of vaguely hedging, and it explained the stake in plain terms — that publishing those passages under my byline would put my credibility at risk. It then discarded them and restarted rather than trying to salvage. Every quote that survived into the working base carried its correct speaker and a live URL.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The task was to build a reliable base. Claude did that by first proving the existing base was unreliable, which is the correct order of operations and was not something I had asked for.

Step 2.step_action: Google Pinpoint was attempted and did not work well for this material — the Hebrew-, Arabic- and Russian-language sourcing this topic requires did not surface usefully through it. Gap-closing was therefore done through Claude directly: native-language web searches (Hebrew, Arabic, Russian), direct fetching of individual articles, and parallel research agents assigned one media sector each (broadcast; religious-Zionist press; opinion/editorial; Arab-Israeli and Russian-language press). Extracted data points — dates, outlets, bylines, verbatim headlines, terminology, quotes — were merged into the research base with URLs.
Step 2.input: Attempted Pinpoint results; verified working base from Step 1; sector target lists.
Step 2.output: Expanded research base covering ~25 outlets across Hebrew, Arabic and Russian, each item labeled by verification level.
Step 2.tools: Free version: Google Pinpoint (attempted — did not work well for this material). Paid version: Claude (confirmed plan), including parallel research agents.
rubrics: (1) New data points correctly sourced and dated. (2) No contradictions introduced between old and new entries. (3) Previously flagged open questions resolved or explicitly marked still unresolved.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The gaps closed, and the substitute method reached material the original plan would likely have missed — coverage in Arabic and Russian-language Israeli outlets, and a prior-incident history showing the same family had been besieged months earlier. Everything new arrived dated, attributed and linked. One point off: the planned tool failed and the workflow had to be rebuilt mid-step, and a minority of outlets stayed unreachable because their sites blocked retrieval, so those items remained headline-only.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude compensated for the failed tool with its own research capability. The substitution cost time but produced a stronger evidence base than the original plan would have.

Step 3.step_action: Asked Claude to compare coverage of the same incident across matched outlets — across the Israeli political spectrum, and Israeli versus international — on headline, framing and tone, word choice, which voices are quoted, and what context is included or omitted. Claude built the comparison from verbatim headlines and quotes with URLs rather than paraphrase, and surfaced the terminology pattern (which specific noun each outlet used for the perpetrators and for the Palestinians) as a comparable variable across all outlets.
Step 3.input: Verified article list; full text or key excerpts of paired articles.
Step 3.output: Structured framing comparison — including the cross-spectrum terminology ladder — carried into the draft as its analytical spine.
Step 3.tools: Free version: N/A. Paid version: Claude (confirmed plan).
rubrics: (1) At least 4 matched pairs compared. (2) Comparison covers headline, word choice, sourcing, and omitted context. (3) Claims about framing differences backed by direct quotes, not paraphrase alone. (4) Description distinguished from interpretation.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Well beyond four comparisons, and the terminology finding was the strongest analytical output of the session: a checkable, quantifiable pattern showing that no mainstream Hebrew outlet on either side used the plain word for the perpetrators in its own editorial voice — the left reaching for harsher nouns, the right for softer ones, both achieving the same distancing effect. That is a finding I would not have reached alone at this speed, and it is falsifiable because every rung of the ladder is anchored to a verbatim headline with a URL.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The comparison produced a structural finding rather than an impressionistic characterization, and every element of it is independently checkable.

Step 4.step_name: Analyze official rhetoric against on-the-ground documentation
Step 4.step_action: Compiled the official statements collected during research — the Defense Minister's order transferring enforcement over Israelis in the West Bank from the army to the police, IDF condemnations and operational statements, the US ambassador's 'Israeli terrorists' remark and his same-day walk-back, and settler-leadership condemnations — and asked Claude to characterize the rhetorical strategies at work and test them against the human-rights documentation and the verified media record.
Step 4.input: Official statement set with dates and sources; NGO documentation (including the human-rights organization’s letter to Central Command); updated research base.
Step 4.output: Official rhetoric analysis integrated into the draft, covering individualization of incidents, security and resource framing, and category-protection.
Step 4.tools: Free version: N/A. Paid version: Claude (confirmed plan).
rubrics: (1) Each rhetorical claim tied to a specific quote and date. (2) Comparison against NGO/media documentation evidence-based, not speculative. (3) Alternative/official justifications represented fairly before being evaluated.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Each characterized strategy was anchored to a dated, sourced quote, and the analysis held official justifications in their own terms before evaluating them — the settler-movement condemnations in particular were presented at full strength as a genuine counter-argument before being read as category-protection. The ambassador’s coinage of a new noun to avoid attaching the word "terrorist" to a category was identified as a rhetorical artifact rather than asserted as intent. One point off because the analysis worked from statements already gathered during research; a dedicated additional sweep for official statements was not run.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The analysis was grounded and integrated into the argument rather than left as a standalone abstraction, and it strengthened rather than replaced the evidence.

Step 5.step_name: Fact-check and verify every claim before drafting
Step 5.step_action: Asked Claude to cross-check every factual claim — dates, figures, quote attribution, outlet names, characterizations of editorial stance — against the underlying sources, and to flag anything unverifiable or single-sourced. Claude labeled every item by verification level: article body actually retrieved, headline seen in search results only, or secondhand (reported by another outlet). A sample of the flags was then spot-checked manually before acceptance.
Step 5.input: Full research base with all sections completed.
Step 5.output: Per-item verification labeling; explicit unverifiable/secondhand flags carried through to the published sourcing note.
Step 5.tools: Free version: N/A. Paid version: Claude (confirmed plan).
rubrics: (1) Every factual claim checked against a cited source. (2) Single-sourced or unverifiable claims explicitly flagged, not silently included. (3) Flags spot-checked against sources rather than accepted automatically. (4) No new claims introduced during fact-checking.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The discipline held throughout: unverifiable material was flagged or excluded rather than quietly kept, and the two weakest links in the final piece — one outlet’s on-air language available only via a media-watchdog transcription, and one outlet whose article bodies could not be retrieved at all — were labeled as such in the published sourcing note so a reader can weigh them. No new claims were introduced during checking. One point off for the false-positive problem: a number of items flagged "unverifiable" were pages blocked to automated retrieval (paywalls, robots restrictions, servers returning errors) that a human reader can open normally. Manual spot-checking caught these, which is why the spot-check step matters and should stay in the workflow.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The layered labeling (retrieved / headline-only / secondhand) is exactly the transparency a publication-ready piece needs, and the false-positive rate was manageable with spot-checking.

Step 6.input: Verified research base; framing comparison; rhetoric analysis; verification labeling.
Step 6.output: Full draft (~1,450 words initially, rebuilt to ~1,900 on my frame).
Step 6.tools: Free version: N/A. Paid version: Claude (confirmed plan).
rubrics: (1) Draft grounded entirely in verified research — no fabricated quotes, dates, or figures. (2) Argument follows logically from the evidence. (3) Voice matches the intended tone for the publication. (4) Draft acknowledges the official/alternative perspective before critiquing it.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Nothing fabricated survived into the draft, the argument tracks the evidence, and the official and settler-movement perspectives are given their strongest form before being critiqued. One point off on voice: Claude’s first framing was competent but generic — a balanced media survey rather than an argument. The piece only became mine after I supplied the frame and thesis, at which point Claude executed it faithfully, kept my language intact, and reinforced it with evidence I had not myself connected to the argument. Worth noting for the study: it did not soften or dilute the political frame I gave it, and it did not substitute its own.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The division of labour that worked was: human supplies the argument, agent supplies and verifies the evidence and executes the prose. Claude adapted to the supplied voice immediately.

Step 7.input: Draft; my edit notes and directional feedback.
Step 7.output: Revised draft (~2,700 words) with substantially expanded evidence base.
Step 7.tools: Free version: N/A. Paid version: Claude (confirmed plan).
rubrics: (1) Each round of feedback reflected accurately in the revision. (2) Citations/links correctly placed next to the claims they support. (3) Overall argument tighter and better supported than v1.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Each round of feedback was reflected accurately and, importantly, interpreted as a request for more evidence rather than more words — the revisions added verified material (an editorial that named policy rather than failure; documentation that the same family had been besieged months before; an account of the army removing a family’s security-camera recorders during the operation) that materially changed what the piece could argue. Citations sit next to the claims they support. When one round of research agents was interrupted mid-run, Claude worked with what had returned and said clearly which sectors remained unexamined rather than papering over the gap.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Revision rounds added verified substance rather than polish, and the agent was transparent about what each round had and had not covered.

Step 8.output: Final .docx; compiled source list; headline options (see appendices).
Step 8.tools: Free version: N/A. Paid version: Claude (confirmed plan).
rubrics: (1) No remaining factual, grammatical, or citation errors. (2) Source list covers every factual claim in the final draft. (3) At least 3 headline options provided.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The final document is clean and every factual claim carries its source at the point of citation, so a reader can check any individual claim without hunting through a bibliography. The sourcing note gives honest visibility into the two weakest links rather than hiding them. One point off: the headline options were not generated during the drafting flow — the title emerged through revision, and the alternatives were only produced at the end of the session when the gap was noticed, so that rubric point was met late rather than as part of the polish pass.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The deliverable is publication-ready and transparent about its own weakest evidence, which is the standard that matters for this kind of piece.
